summary:
AstroVital is a health tracking app that helps astronauts keep their body and mind healthy while they float in space. AstroVital gives data on sleep, exercise, and body movement showing how the body changes in microgravity and how to stay healthy. The dashboard records movement, mobility, and recovery over time and a points system rewards good habits and regular use.

The health section gives a body check, including heart rate and AI bone density check from medical pictures. The mobility section watches shoulders, hips, ankles, spine, hamstrings and balance. The recovery section gives an improvement score. Daily reminders push wellness routines. An AI helper answers questions and gives personal advice. The crew section lets astronauts connect, compare data and talk with teammates. The reminders also help everyone know how they are doing and if they need assistance 

AstroVital tackles the dangers of space trips, like muscle loss, bone weakening and bad sleep by turning hard health data into clear useful tips. Because astronaut health directly affects mission success. AstroVital is a tool and it also helps mental health with community and motivation. AstroVital helps everyone stay together in a community while progressing their health in space.
details:
Astro Vital is an application to log health metrics used to track astronauts' health and is already integrated with Apple Health for sleep, exercise and movement data. This data can then be analysed to assess if their bodies are adapting to microgravity. There is a dashboard to track movement, mobility and recovery. There is a points system to incentivise good health habits. Within the health section you can track the entire body, heart rate and bone density analysis via medical image AI. The mobility section can track shoulder, hip, ankle mobility, spinal mobility, hamstring mobility and balance. The recovery section calculates a score based on your progress. There is a daily prompt reminder to keep you on top of your health, an AI assistant to give personal advice and a crew section to connect with friends and family.

This application assists astronauts in detecting problems early, for example, muscle atrophy, bone loss or sleeping problems. It also assists mental well-being by maintaining motivation levels and assisting in socializing with others. Since an astronaut's health may have an effect on the overall success of the mission, our goal was to keep them fit, linked and focused.

All the apps were developed in JavaScript, HTML and CSS. Bone density analysis and the AI Assistant was powered by Claude. Space data was supplied by the NASA API. The app design was created in Canva.

We concentrated on streamlining the health data for the crew. We needed to make sure the app was simple and clear to follow, especially since they are busy and working in a special environment. We implemented a points system and a daily prompt to ensure each user was motivated and on track. We created a crew section to address the problem of going to space with friends and isolation, to aid the mental health of the crew. The app is compatible with Apple Watch, iPhone, iPad, and computer. We ensured that the app was accessible for many different needs including the space element. We considered the sensitive nature of the health data.
